description: Say where the calls go: the board that receives one row per call, which column gets which call field, and, optionally, how a call is linked to a customer (by the other party's phone number, Israeli numbers compared in one normal form: 05x, +9725x, 9725x) and to an employee (by the extension number). Replaces the whole mapping. Column ids from get_board_schema; the boards must be in the app's project. Call fields: externalId (the PBX call id, map it to keep rows traceable), direction, from, to, extension, agentName, startedAt, answeredAt, endedAt (ISO UTC times, use date/datetime columns), durationSec, talkSec (numbers), status, hangupBy. direction and status are written as Hebrew words (נכנסת/יוצאת, נענתה/לא נענתה/תפוס/נכשלה); for a dropdown or status column whose options differ, set labels. customer: { boardId (the customers board), matchColumnId (its phone column), linkColumnId (a relation column on the calls board) }. employee: the same with the extension column of the employees board. A phone or extension that two rows share is not linked (never guessed). startDate (YYYY-MM-DD) is where the first sync starts, default 7 days back. Syncing happens in the background once the server runs the telephony worker; run_telephony_sync does it now. Owner or admin of the app.

appId.description: App id or slug (from list_apps / create_app)

boardId.description: The board that receives a row per call

columns.description: Call field -> column id on the board. At least one

customer.description: Link calls to customers by phone

employee.description: Link calls to employees by extension

labels.description: Text written for direction and status, to match a closed-choice column's options

organizationId.description: Organization id; defaults to the credential organization when omitted

name: configure_telephony_mapping
